In [[group theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''commutator collecting process''' is a method for writing an element of a [[group (mathematics)|group]] as a product of generators and their higher [[commutator]]s arranged in a certain order. The commutator collecting process was introduced by [[Philip Hall]] in 1934<ref>
{{Citation | last1=Hall | first1=Philip | author1-link=Philip Hall | title=A contribution to the theory of groups of prime-power order | year=1934 | journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society | volume=36 | pages=29–95 | doi=10.1112/plms/s2-36.1.29}}
</ref> and articulated by [[Wilhelm Magnus]] in 1937.<ref>
W. Magnus (1937), "Über Beziehungen zwischen höheren Kommutatoren", ''J. Grelle'' '''177''', 105-115.
</ref>  The process is sometimes called a "collection process".

The process can be generalized to define a [[totally ordered]] subset of a free non-associative algebra, that is, a [[free magma]]; this subset is called the [[Hall set]]. Members of the Hall set are [[binary trees]]; these can be placed in one-to-one correspondence with words, these being called the [[Hall word]]s; the [[Lyndon word]]s are a special case.  Hall sets are used to construct a basis for a [[free Lie algebra]], entirely analogously to the commutator collecting process. Hall words also provide a unique [[monoid factorisation|factorization of monoids]].

==Statement==

The commutator collecting process is usually stated for [[free group]]s, as a similar theorem then holds for any group by writing it as a [[quotient group|quotient]] of a free group. 

Suppose ''F''<sub>1</sub> is a free group on generators ''a''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''a''<sub>''m''</sub>. Define the descending [[central series]] by putting
:''F''<sub>''n''+1</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;[''F''<sub>''n''</sub>,&nbsp;''F''<sub>1</sub>]
The basic commutators are elements of ''F''<sub>1</sub> defined and ordered as follows:
*The basic commutators of weight 1 are the [[group generators|generators]] ''a''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''a''<sub>''m''</sub>.
*The basic commutators of weight ''w''&nbsp;>&nbsp;1 are the elements [''x'',&nbsp;''y''] where ''x'' and ''y'' are basic commutators whose weights sum to ''w'', such that ''x''&nbsp;>&nbsp;''y'' and if ''x''&nbsp;=&nbsp;[''u'',&nbsp;''v''] for basic commutators ''u'' and ''v'' then ''v''&nbsp;&le;&nbsp;''y''. 
Commutators are ordered so that ''x''&nbsp;>&nbsp;''y'' if ''x'' has weight greater than that of ''y'', and for commutators of any fixed weight some total ordering is chosen. 
 
Then ''F''<sub>''n''</sub> / ''F''<sub>''n''+1</sub> is a [[finitely generated abelian group|finitely generated free abelian group]] with a basis consisting of basic commutators of weight&nbsp;''n''.

Then any element of ''F'' can be written as

:<math>g=c_1^{n_1}c_2^{n_2}\cdots c_k^{n_k}c</math>

where the ''c''<sub>''i''</sub> are the basic commutators of weight at most ''m'' arranged in order, and ''c'' is a product of commutators of weight greater than ''m'', and the ''n''<sub>''i''</sub> are [[integer]]s.
